hints: Focus on what lower temperature does to both the speed of the reaction and the final equilibrium position.
The forward reaction is exothermic with $\Delta H^\ominus = -9.6$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, so think about which way Le Chatelier shifts equilibrium on cooling.
Combine a slower fall from 0.5 with a final mole fraction of $\text{I}_2$ below 0.23 to pick the curve that is both slower and shifted to more product.
walkthrough:
**Check the starting point**

All experiments start with equal amounts of $\text{H}_2(g)$ and $\text{I}_2(g)$ and no $\text{HI}(g)$. That is why the mole fraction of $\text{I}_2$ starts at 0.5 in every graph.

$$\text{initial mole fraction of I}_2 = 0.5$$

**Use temperature to predict the rate**

Lower temperature $T_2$ means particles have less kinetic energy and fewer successful collisions per second. So the curve must fall more slowly and take longer to flatten out.

$$\text{lower } T \rightarrow \text{slower rate} \rightarrow \text{shallower gradient}$$

**Use Le Chatelier to predict the position**

The equation is $\text{H}_2(g) + \text{I}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI}(g)$ with negative $\Delta H^\ominus$. The forward reaction gives out heat, so cooling favours the forward reaction.

$$\text{decrease } T \rightarrow \text{shift right} \rightarrow \text{less I}_2 \text{ left at equilibrium}$$

**Pick the matching graph**

We need the same start at 0.5, a slower decrease than at $T_1$, and a final plateau below 0.23. Only that combination shows both the kinetic effect and the equilibrium shift correctly.

options.A: Starts at 0.5 and is slower, which is correct for lower T, but it levels off at the same 0.23. This ignores the equilibrium shift to the right for an exothermic forward reaction.
options.B: Correct because it shows both effects. The slower fall shows the lower rate at T2, and the final plateau below 0.23 shows more $\text{HI}$ and less $\text{I}_2$ as equilibrium shifts forward on cooling.
options.C: Shows the same equilibrium value of 0.23 but reaches it faster. Higher temperature would speed up the reaction, not lower temperature, and there is no shift in position here.
options.D: Shows a slower reaction but levels off above 0.23, meaning more $\text{I}_2$ left. That would be a shift to the left, which happens on heating, not cooling, for this exothermic forward reaction.
